molecular_glues.abstract: Mathematics > Rings and Algebras arXiv:2610.18643 (math) [Submitted on 13 Oct 2026] Title: Okubo algebras and Exceptional Periodicity: tetracode gradings, root-lattice obstructions and Clifford cones Authors: Alessio Marrani , Daniele Corradetti View a PDF of the paper titled Okubo algebras and Exceptional Periodicity: tetracode gradings, root-lattice obstructions and Clifford cones, by Alessio Marrani and 1 other authors View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: The Okubo algebra brings together ternary gradings, integral root frames and rank-three geometry. We examine how these structures extend to the complex Exceptional Periodicity algebras. With $N=4(n+1)$, a tetracode character gives eight nonzero homogeneous components of dimension $t_n=8n+3+2^{4n}$. On a tip, a compatible grading has zero component of dimension $8n-5$ and eight nonzero components of dimension $1+2^{4n-3}$. The arithmetic behaves differently: for $n\geq2$, the lattice $D_N^+$ has no full-rank orthogonal frame of unscaled $A_2$ lattices. We exhibit failures of the Jacobi and Jordan identities and determine the derivations and full automorphism group of the ambient algebra above level one. We also give a Clifford-module proof, with the normalization fixed by root products, of the published realization of EP tips as special Vinberg $H$-algebras. This identifies a positive real form and yields explicit formulas for its cone, cubic, Cholesky coordinates and rational dual invariant. The cone is symmetric exactly at $n=1$. Its determinant-one hypersurface belongs to the known $L(8n,1,0)$ series, whose $r$- and $c$-maps give homogeneous scalar manifolds for supergravity theories with eight real supercharges. Abstract The minimal number of inputs in the local function of a non-trivial cellular automaton is two. Such a function can be viewed as as a kind of binary operation. If this operation is associative, it forms, together with the set of states, a semigroup. There are 18 semigroups of order 3 up to equivalence, and they define 18 cellular automata rules with three states. We investigate these rules with respect to solvability and show that all of them are solvable, meaning that the state of a given cell after n iterations can be expressed by an explicit formula. We derive the relevant formulae for all 18 rules using some additional properties possessed by particular semigroups of order 3, such as commutativity and idempotence.
